## Excel Examples {#sec-excel-examples}

**maidr** reads the charts of an Excel workbook. Pass an `.xlsx` or `.xlsm`
file to `maidr.read_excel_charts()`, and hand any chart it returns to
`maidr.show()`, `maidr.render()` or `maidr.save_html()`: the chart can then be
read from the keyboard, as sound, as text and in braille. Excel does not need to
be installed. For charts drawn in Python, see the
[Matplotlib / Seaborn](examples.qmd), [Plotly](examples-plotly.qmd),
[Bokeh](examples-bokeh.qmd), [plotnine](examples-plotnine.qmd) and
[Altair](examples-altair.qmd) pages.

::: {.callout-warning title="Experimental"}
Excel support is **experimental**. What it reads, and how, may change without a
deprecation period, whichever chart type is read: see
[Plot Type Stability](stability.qmd#excel-support).
:::

Every chart Excel saves keeps a copy of the values it drew inside the file, and
**maidr** reads that copy, so the reader hears the numbers the chart shows; the
cells are read only where a file has no copy, as some programs other than Excel
write them. Each chart is then drawn again with matplotlib, in the workbook's
own colors and with its own titles, and the mark being read is outlined on that
drawing. The drawing is not Excel's picture of the chart: fonts and effects
differ.

| Excel chart | read as |
|---|---|
| Column or bar, one series | bar |
| Clustered column or bar | dodged bar |
| Stacked and 100% stacked column or bar | stacked bar; 100% stacked reads each segment's share |
| Line, with or without markers | line, one series per line |
| Pie and doughnut | pie, clockwise from the top |
| Scatter | point; with lines, line |
| Combo, including a second value axis | one layer per chart type in one chart |
| Area, stacked and 100% stacked area | area [experimental], stacked area [experimental] |

Stacked line, radar, bubble, stock, surface and pie-of-pie charts, and the chart
types Excel 2016 added (histogram, Pareto, box and whisker, waterfall, funnel,
treemap, sunburst and map), are left out with a warning naming the chart and its
sheet.

An axis Excel draws no title on is named after the header cell above its
categories, such as *Quarter*: you hear it, and the drawing leaves it off as
Excel does. A value axis keeps its number format, so a percentage reads as one.
Dates read the way the cells show them. A category with no label reads
*(blank)*, and a blank value is a gap, never a zero.

The examples read [sales.xlsx](sales.xlsx), a workbook with one sheet of
quarterly sales and five charts.

### Reading a Workbook

`maidr.read_excel_charts()` returns the charts sheet by sheet and, on each
sheet, top to bottom and left to right, each with the sheet it is on, its name
and its title.

```{python}
#| warning: false
import maidr

charts = maidr.read_excel_charts("sales.xlsx")
for chart in charts:
    print(chart.sheet, chart.name, chart.title, sep=" | ")
```

Save every chart of a workbook as its own page with a loop:

```python
for chart in maidr.read_excel_charts("sales.xlsx"):
    maidr.save_html(chart, f"{chart.name}.html")
```

`maidr.read_excel_charts()` also takes an open binary file, such as the one a
Streamlit or Shiny upload control hands you.

### Clustered Column Chart

Each region is a series and each quarter a category: the left and right arrow
keys move between quarters, and up and down between the regions.

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Clustered column chart of revenue by quarter for the North and South regions
maidr.show(charts[0])
```

### Line Chart

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Line chart of revenue by quarter, one line per region
maidr.show(charts[1])
```

### Pie Chart

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Pie chart of the North region's revenue by quarter
maidr.show(charts[2])
```

### Combo Chart on Two Axes

North's revenue is drawn as columns and its margin as a line on a second value
axis. The two are layers of one chart: Page Up and Page Down move between them.
The margin is read as a percentage, because its cells are formatted as one.

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Column chart of the North region's revenue with a line of its margin on a second axis
maidr.show(charts[3])
```

### Stacked Area Chart [experimental]

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Stacked area chart of revenue by quarter for the North and South regions
maidr.show(charts[4])
```
